results.corrected_extracted: The review prints 89% female and infers probable female predisposition from its case table. Editors' recount is 46/52=88.4615%, or 88.5% to one decimal; this differs from the printed 89%, with no alternate author denominator inferred. If two probable duplicate female rows are omitted, the conditional recount is 44/50=88.0%, not a verified distinct-patient sample. results.note: Person-first wording replacement confirmed against the original review, rereading Section 5.1.5 on p. 11 and the Ayus 1992 reference on p. 12. The approximately 25-times comparison is conditional on encephalopathy in the p. 11 passage; the postoperative setting is identified by the p. 12 reference title rather than that body passage. The nearby hormonal and muscle-mass discussion draws on physiology and animal work and does not describe a test of those explanations in people taking MDMA. The replacement changes only the requested phrase, preserving the postoperative setting, second-hand status and prohibition on treating this as an MDMA susceptibility multiplier. Primary reports and experiments remain unread.
results.corrected_extracted: The review reports that, once hyponatraemic encephalopathy develops, menstruant women were about 25 times as likely to die or have permanent brain injury as men or postmenopausal women (Ayus 1992). The reference title on p.12 identifies postoperative patients, not people who take MDMA. Other proposed hormonal and muscle-mass explanations are drawn from physiology/animal work rather than a test of those explanations in people taking MDMA; primary reports were not read.
